why: It is 'measure, then cut': commit 2 runs only if the Lighthouse table shows fonts as the largest wait, commit 3 only if a themed page fetches more than one woff2 per family, commit 4 only if a cart prefetch at load is found by a search the brief could not do, and stop_if 2 hands the choice of a script or stylesheet step to someone else. Which cut to make is decided by readings that do not exist yet.
harm_if_wrong: A wrong font preload or subset cut slows the first paint or shows a fallback font on stores; a mis-delayed prefetch makes the cart slower to open.
brief_problems: stop_if 2 ends '[an executor] should choose it', a redacted placeholder.
Commit 4 creates/extends e2e/prefetch.spec.ts 'made by step 1.3' without knowing its shape, and does not name the prefetch to delay.
